exceptions.local_invariant: Anchor identifiers are unique within one review result.
exceptions.provider_evidence: JSON Schema array uniqueness compares complete objects and cannot express uniqueness of one property across otherwise distinct anchor objects.

exceptions.local_invariant: A finding identifier is unique within each event array; a new finding may pair only with one closing status change.
exceptions.provider_evidence: The supported writer subset has no cross-array relation and cannot compare finding_id properties across generated array items.

exceptions.local_invariant: New finding identifiers start at next_finding_id and remain contiguous in canonical order.
exceptions.provider_evidence: Claude Code 2.1.241 rejects prefixItems, so the schema closes the finite ID window but local validation retains ordering and contiguity.

exceptions.local_invariant: The response request_id equals the request identifier whose digest includes the response-schema digest.
exceptions.provider_evidence: Embedding the final request_id as a schema const would change the response-schema digest in the request_id preimage; exact equality therefore remains local.

exceptions.local_invariant: A denial leaves an own BLOCKER open; an approval leaves no own BLOCKER open and no open Finding in the current Slice after every finding transition is applied.
exceptions.provider_evidence: The writer schema constrains each event and cardinality but cannot fold prior finding state together with generated status changes.

exceptions.local_invariant: Every open finding is disposed exactly once in canonical order.
exceptions.provider_evidence: Codex 0.147.0 rejects prefixItems and array-valued const; minItems/maxItems plus an ID enum close membership and cardinality only.

exceptions.local_invariant: Human rationale and self-check fields are non-blank and NUL-free.
exceptions.provider_evidence: Codex Structured Outputs rejects the safe-text positive lookahead; local domain validation remains authoritative.

exceptions.local_invariant: The response request_id equals the request identifier whose digest includes the response-schema digest.
exceptions.provider_evidence: Embedding the final request_id as a schema const would change the response-schema digest that is itself part of the request_id preimage; the format remains schema-bound and exact equality remains local.

exceptions.local_invariant: Repository paths are relative, traversal-free, canonical POSIX paths outside .orchestrator.
exceptions.provider_evidence: Codex Structured Outputs rejects regex lookaround and uniqueItems; the writer projection removes only those unsupported keywords.

exceptions.local_invariant: Planned Slice identifiers are contiguous and one-based, and every Slice carries repository paths in sorted canonical order.
exceptions.provider_evidence: Codex 0.147.0 rejects prefixItems and array-valued const. A Slice-3 live Canary consequently produced writer-valid Slice ID 03 for a one-Slice plan; the provider subset can neither bind generated array positions to contiguous identifiers nor compare adjacent generated path values lexicographically.

exceptions.local_invariant: Stop remediation paths are sorted in canonical repository order.
exceptions.provider_evidence: Codex 0.147.0 rejects prefixItems and array-valued const, so JSON Schema cannot compare adjacent generated path values lexicographically.

exceptions.local_invariant: Reported test files are sorted in canonical repository order for fixed and dynamic test scopes.
exceptions.provider_evidence: Codex 0.147.0 rejects prefixItems and array-valued const, so JSON Schema can close membership and cardinality but cannot compare adjacent generated path values lexicographically.

exceptions.local_invariant: A new finding signature differs from every earlier new finding in the same result; a unique match to an offered open finding is coalesced into that finding as an occurrence, while ambiguous or contradictory matches are rejected.
exceptions.provider_evidence: The supported JSON Schema subset cannot derive NFKC/casefolded SHA-256 values from generated acceptance prose and repository-path mentions, compare candidates with one another, or prove that a known-signature match has one lossless offered occurrence target.
